feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/strategic blend is compelling. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and broad platform/tool expertise.  
- Writing is professional and readable, with a consistent leadership narrative across digital strategy, governance, content operations, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would sharpen structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-driven achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results such as growth %, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, or cost savings would increase impact.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without final commas); standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper value proposition would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, cross-channel strategy, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a more concise, executive-level framing.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web modernization, cross-channel content operations, and audience-focused communications for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital governance, editorial workflow design, and platform strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear content, aligning stakeholders, and building systems that improve reach, coordination, and execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Building workflows and systems” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are already reinforced elsewhere; keep them concise here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “CMS and web operations,” “Editorial systems and governance.”
- Replace vague items like “Multi-channel communication” and “Workflow & systems architecture” with more specific, senior-level language tied to your experience.
- Consider grouping related ideas to reduce list fatigue and improve scanability.
- Suggested version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS and web operations • Editorial systems and governance • Analytics, reporting and optimization • Content systems and workflow design • Stakeholder and cross-functional alignment • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats the header and Soft Skills section.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay broad, not tool-specific.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new in the consultant remit and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, content operations, and enterprise web modernization for its public-facing communications ecosystem.”
- Combine overlapping duties into 3–4 impact bullets; emphasize consultant-level value: strategy, Drupal experience design, governance, and AI search.
- Replace generic verbs (“build,” “deliver,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “streamlined,” “designed,” “launched,” “improved,” “standardized.”
- Add measurable scope if available: number of sites/templates/toolkits launched, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, stakeholder teams supported, or traffic/user adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance/usability best practices” repeat themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a specific project or result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize transformation and scale:
- “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”
- “Implemented enterprise analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting and decision-making.”
- “Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve operational consistency.”
- If possible, add outcome metrics for email/social growth, reporting efficiency, cost savings, or production volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing execution-level leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before you owned strategy/governance at the director level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and start with actions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is repeated in multiple NACo roles; vary the framing here.
- “weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; clarify what expanded or changed at this level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, outcome-oriented positioning, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, workflow design & publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging for complex stakeholders
- Audience-centered content strategy, information architecture & campaign planning
- Consider adding one stronger differentiator from recent work, such as “AI-enabled search and content discovery strategy” if you want this section to feel more current.
- Keep wording parallel: use noun phrases with consistent structure, not mixed concepts.
- If space is tight, cut “audience-focused content planning,” which is the least distinctive.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” also repeats achievements already demonstrated in the 2022–Present NACo entries.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value capabilities and group tools more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as capability-led, not list-led: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep AI-enabled search, since both are strongly supported by the most recent roles.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer impact-oriented phrasing like “front-end implementation” or “content platform delivery.”
- If space allows, add one outcome cue: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large-scale public-facing web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave specific tools like Power Automate, Zapier, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, etc. to Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT; avoid repeating it elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for your most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating analytics language already covered in Core Competencies and the Director role.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for KPI design, executive reporting, and digital performance optimization.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “executive dashboarding” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Consider tightening “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and conversion analysis” if accurate; it’s more specific and modern.
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics platforms: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • KPI design • Executive dashboarding • SEO, UX, and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; this item should emphasize tools and applied outcomes instead.
- The Director role already names these platforms, so avoid repeating the exact same sequence elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with work-experience bullets that already show studio buildout, livestreams, and video production. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery, not just tools: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the in-house studio achievement.
- If space allows, make it more outcomes-oriented: “Studio and livestream production for advocacy programming, virtual events, and recurring multimedia content.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad categories with narrow tools unless the tool is a differentiator.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming,” “studio operations,” and “video production” are already evidenced in NACo roles; this skills line should summarize, not repeat.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, lead with it and consider trimming lower-signal items unless they are job-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if your use was limited; it can read as less strategic than the rest.
- Keep formatting parallel with other technical items; avoid repeating implementation details already covered under Coding & Technical Execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t add that phrase here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic terms unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied capability, not just languages/tools: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner, more current phrasing.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent roles, e.g. “for Drupal-based public websites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”
- Put strongest/recently used tools first; if GTM is used more than jQuery now, move it ahead of jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations…”). Differentiate this section as tools/platforms only, or cut repeated items there.
- “Workflow automation” already appears elsewhere; avoid implying the same capability here unless tied to GitHub Actions specifically.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design expertise. Since the CV already emphasizes systems architecture and automation, this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier”
- Separate project/work management from collaboration tools: “Project systems: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp” / “Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the actual content.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams may feel low-value unless grouped as collaboration tools rather than presented as core technical systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize system depth or be tightened to avoid over-weighting older/basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add level/context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign orchestration, segmentation, journeys) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)**
- Keep naming consistent and concise; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 CI/Journeys** if space is tight.
- If one platform was central in recent work, place it first and consider dropping the least relevant/oldest tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating “email strategy” language here.
- If Higher Logic or Dynamics were not used recently or materially, listing them may dilute stronger, more current technical strengths.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful team-building context, but the bullet is broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-stage digital buildout.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows for web, email, social media, and multimedia production.”
- Add clearer outputs: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or publishing volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or first producing the series.
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with multiple later roles; frame this as initial process setup rather than broader operational leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, translating findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast the headline achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a two-bullet format for clarity rather than one blended paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid generic “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing; later roles already cover broad multimedia work more strongly.
- Don’t overemphasize digital leadership here, since that progression is better demonstrated in 2015–2024 roles.
